chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Ibn Bukayr from Ubayd Allah al-Halabi said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A woman gave birth from zina (unlawful sexual intercourse); should I take her as a wet-nurse? He said: Do not have her wet-nurse, nor her daughter.

key_terms.تَسْتَرْضِعْهَا: Have her wet-nurse (take her as a wet-nurse)

ai.seo_question: Is a woman who gave birth from zina permissible to be a wet-nurse in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a woman who gives birth from zina is suitable to be a wet-nurse (radha'), and her daughter is also permissible, countering the view that the father's status affects the milk's validity. This ruling emphasizes that the biological act of nursing establishes the foster relationship regardless of the father's lineage, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding *radha'* (fosterage). The narration highlights the practical application of lineage rules, ensuring that the child's status is not negatively impacted by the mother's marital or sexual history in terms of nursing eligibility.
